messages:
ashley_support: Customer (AcmePayments) opened a ticket: their webhook consumer is failing when we return a function/tool call result. They say amount is missing and their system rejects the invoice. Repro attached. Can eng triage? :rotating_light:

matt_engineer: Thanks, Ashley. Can you drop the exact request_id and payload? Also which model + schema did they use?

ashley_support: request_id=rc-20260315-9a8b, model=redwood/chat-1, function=createInvoice (declared schema below). Customer says our response JSON has a shape mismatch. They pasted the response: ```{
  "invoiceId": "inv_123",
  "line_items": [{"desc": "Consulting"}],
  "status": "created"
}``` Missing amount under line_items entries. They claim our function call returned a truncated object.

matt_engineer: Reproducing locally now. Can you confirm if their code uses structured_output=true or function calling?

ashley_support: They used function calling + JSON mode (we auto-serialize function args). We see a 200 from the API but their consumer fails JSON.parse on our payload.

runtime_bot: Pod inference-rw-12 on us-west-2 restarted 2m before rc-20260315-9a8b was processed. Crash reason: OOM during KV cache compaction. Trace id: tr-77c4.

matt_engineer: OOM might've truncated streaming buffer. Please paste the exact raw HTTP response body from our logs (not the parsed object).

ashley_support: Raw response (from customer-provided capture): ```HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"invoiceId":"inv_123","line_items":[{"desc":"Consulting"}],"status":"created"}``` (same as above).

matt_engineer: Thanks. Our expected function schema for createInvoice is: ```params: {
  type: object,
  properties: {
    invoiceId: {type: string},
    line_items: {
      type: array,
      items: {type: object, properties: {desc: {type: string}, amount: {type: number}}, required:["desc","amount"]}
    },
    status: {type: string}
  },
  required: ["invoiceId","line_items","status"]
}```

dinesh_oncall: I pulled the service logs for rc-20260315-9a8b. The runtime attempted to stream function args out but encountered an exception in the serializer: `KeyError: 'amount'` inside our post-processing validator while applying schema-required checks during finalization. Stack excerpt: ```File "serializer.py", line 412, in finalize
  v = obj['amount']
KeyError: 'amount'``` Looks like a bug: our post-serialization validator is reading keys before fallback defaults are applied.

olivia_prodeng: Is that the validator that runs in the router after streaming completes? If OOM happened it might have left a partial buffer and validator attempted to access missing keys leading to a hard failure instead of returning a well-formed error. Any evidence of partial write to response stream?

matt_engineer: I see two things: (1) on memory pressure we currently don't atomically swap the serialized payload from staging to final buffer, so a truncated final buffer can be emitted; (2) the validator code assumes `amount` exists and raises instead of returning a structured validation error. Both are bugs.

ashley_support: Customer wants an ETA and asks whether they were charged for the failed webhook. Billing check? :money_with_wings:

billing_bot: For request rc-20260315-9a8b the billing pipeline marked the call as SUCCESS and billed per-token. However we have a charge dispute flow. If engineering determines the response was malformed due to our runtime bug, we can issue a credit. Please escalate to SRE/Engineering.

matt_engineer: Action plan: 1) Create a small patch to make validator defensive (return structured 4xx with validation errors instead of throwing). 2) Add atomic swap for final serialized payload to prevent partial emits on OOM. 3) Add an integration test that streams a large KV cache to reproduce OOM and ensure serializer never emits half JSON. Assigning owner: matt_engineer.

dinesh_oncall: Oncall note: I restarted inference-rw-12 and bumped pod memory temporarily to mitigate recurrence. Kept crash artifacts under /var/log/runtime/crash-archives/tr-77c4 .

matt_engineer: I'll open a PR with the validator fix and tests. Short-term mitigation: patch router to detect malformed JSON responses (quick parse check) and return 502 so billing is not marked success. I'll coordinate with billing to reverse charge if needed.

ashley_support: Thanks. Customer accepted temporary workaround (we configured them to retry on parse errors) but wants a permanent fix. Please keep me updated so I can reply with ETA.

matt_engineer: ETA for validator fix and tests: ~4 business days. Hotfix for parse-check mitigation: 6-12 hours. I'll post PR link when available.

olivia_prodeng: Also add a regression guard in our rollout: make sure function-calling schema test runs against canary traffic.

matt_engineer: Will do. Adding ticket RN-3142 and will add postmortem once fixed. @ashley_support I will update by EOD with PR/rollback plan. :thumbsup:
